test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The movie 'Chak De India' is based on which real-life Indian sports figure's story?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mir Ranjan Negi**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The 2007 Bollywood film **Chak De! India**, starring **Shah Rukh Khan**, is heavily inspired by the life and redemption arc of **Mir Ranjan Negi**, a former goalkeeper for the **Indian national field hockey team**.

• The movie's narrative parallels Negi's real-life experience during the **1982 Asian Games** final against **Pakistan**, where India suffered a devastating **1−7** loss. Following the defeat, Negi faced intense public scrutiny and baseless allegations of **match-fixing**.

• Mirroring the character **Kabir Khan**, Negi returned to the sport as a coach to clear his name. He served as the **goalkeeping coach** for the **1998 Asian Games** gold-medal-winning men's team and the **2002 Commonwealth Games** gold-medal-winning women's team.

• The victory of the **Indian Women's Hockey Team** at the **2002 Commonwealth Games** in Manchester provided the primary thematic backdrop for the film's climactic success.

• **Mir Ranjan Negi** was directly involved in the film's production as a **technical consultant**, training the actors to ensure authentic hockey gameplay on screen.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Dilip Tirkey**:

• He is a legendary **defender** and former captain, known as the **'The Wall'** of Indian hockey for his exceptional defensive skills.

• He holds the record for the most **international appearances** (412 caps) for India and was a recipient of the **Padma Shri** and **Arjuna Award**.

• **Dhanraj Pillay**:

• An iconic **forward**, he is the only player to have competed in four **Olympic Games**, four **World Cups**, and four **Asian Games**.

• He served as the captain of the national team and received India's highest sporting honor, the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna**.

• **Balbir Singh Sr.**:

• A three-time **Olympic gold medalist** (1948, 1952, 1956), he is regarded as one of the greatest **center-forwards** in hockey history.

• He coached the Indian team to its only **World Cup** title in 1975.
